name: Collective Numeral Construction

dimensions.form: Plural cardinal noun in PP, often coordinated (twos and threes)
dimensions.meaning: Grouping or distribution by numerical size
dimensions.function: Specifies manner of grouping or arrangement
dimensions.distribution: Adverbial PP modifying manner of action

1.definition: Cardinal nouns denote group sizes for collective arrangement

examples.note: Magnitude reading, often large numbers rather than batches of exactly one hundred

constraints.description: Cardinal noun is a common noun; takes plural morphology.

projection.target: People entered in threes can describe an arbitrarily large crowd. Three counts the members in each group even though threes is itself grammatically plural. A phrase such as by the hundreds can instead indicate large numbers without fixed groups.
projection.evidence: Reynolds assigns the grouping use its own semantic role among cardinal nouns. The constructed contrast checks whether the number applies to the total or to the groups.

curious.title: Counting and arranging in groups
curious.summary: A plural number word after in or by can tell how people or things are grouped.
curious.body:
In twos and threes describes people arriving or being arranged in small groups. The number tells the size of each group, not the total. People entered in threes could be an enormous crowd, since three counts the members of each group.

Count by fives uses a number for grouping too. By the hundreds works a little differently. It suggests large numbers, not batches of exactly one hundred.
curious.try: Say People entered in threes. Does three tell you how many people there were in all, or how many in each group?

teacher.summary: Useful for explaining plural number words that give group sizes after in or by.
teacher.explain: In this construction a plural cardinal noun in a PP with in or by gives the size of groups, and the PP is an adverbial modifying the manner of the action (arriving in twos and threes). The cardinal noun is a common noun and takes plural morphology. Three counts the members of each group even though threes is grammatically plural. By the hundreds works differently: it can indicate large numbers without fixed groups, rather than batches of exactly one hundred.
teacher.terms: Cardinal noun: a number word used as a noun. Compare a cardinal determinative, as in three people.

contrasts.note: Three counts the members of each group; the crowd can be of any size.

watch_for: A learner might read in threes as a total of three people.
A learner might read by the hundreds as batches of exactly one hundred.
teacher.activity: Students line up in twos, then in threes, and describe what happened using in twos and in threes. They then count aloud by fives and say what the number tells them.

child.explain: A number can tell how big each group is. In twos means two at a time. Count by fives means you jump five each time.
child.play: Line up your friends in twos, then in threes. Say what you did with in twos and in threes.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Collective Numeral Construction." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/collective-numeral-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, fa37529).
